memorial_details: Small blue circular plaque with central illustration of a Lancaster in flight, set into a large stone. White coloured inscription, names, drawing and border edgings.
narrative: On 6 March 1945, Lancaster PB475 departed RAF Little Staughton at 17:33 on a bombing raid to Chemnitz. On the return flight, a hung-up target indicator ignited in the bomb bay. The aircraft crashed at 01:00 near Bloomfield Farm, Bellingdon, Buckinghamshire. Six of the seven crew were killed. The sole survivor was tail gunner Bill Heart.
inscription:
Six young airmen
died at this spot on
6 March 1945.
Participants in, and victims of the
human preoccupation with war.
Great lives cut short
Royal Air Force
(3 Names)
Royal Australian Air Force
(3 Names)
We remember them.
